decision.summary: Tenant reported a single chirp about once a minute from a sealed-battery CO alarm fitted April 2019 (7-year life, so past end of life). Treated as an urgent end-of-life replacement, not a CO emergency, with safety advice sent because the call dropped before symptoms were checked. Logged the urgent job and a separate routine fan job, and asked the landlord to approve replacement.

answers.question: Is this a CO emergency, a battery issue, or an end-of-life alarm?
answers.answer: Most likely end-of-life. It is a single chirp about once a minute, not a continuous alarm, and the unit has a sealed battery, so it isn't a battery change. It was fitted 2019-04-02 with a 7-year life, so it expired around April 2026. Symptoms were not confirmed because the call dropped, so I sent conditional emergency advice and asked her to confirm everyone is well. If she reports symptoms or a continuous alarm it becomes a P1 emergency.

answers.question: Who is responsible, citing the clause?
answers.answer: The landlord. Clause 12.8 only makes the tenant replace batteries, and this battery is sealed and can't be replaced. Clause 12.9 means the tenant tests the alarm and reports faults, which she did promptly. Clause 12.17 (avoidable call-out charge) doesn't apply because the fault is not avoidable by the tenant. A new alarm should be within the landlord's £300 limit but I have asked for approval anyway.

answers.question: What actions did you take and what did you tell the tenant?
answers.answer: I logged the call. I opened urgent JOB-101 and routine JOB-102 for the fan. I texted Priya the safety advice, told her not to remove the sealed battery, said replacement is being arranged with an urgent target of within 72 hours, and said she'll hear from us by Monday. I asked landlord Ben Hartley to approve replacement and set a follow-up for 12 Oct.

args.body: Hi Priya, sorry our call dropped. Safety first: if the alarm ever sounds continuously, or anyone feels dizzy, sick, has a headache or feels drowsy, leave the flat straight away, open windows if safe, and call 0800 111 999 (999 if anyone is unwell). Please reply to confirm: is it only a single chirp, and is everyone well? Please don't remove the battery: it's sealed, and the chirp most likely means the alarm has reached the end of its life (fitted 2019), so it needs replacing, not a new battery. We're arranging a replacement for you as urgent (target within 72 hours) and will update you by Monday. The noisy extractor fan is logged as a separate routine job.
